releases.notes:
# BPB VPN v1.3.0

This release introduces some important improvements like VLESS DNS compatibility and improvements, fallback DNS servers while using Exit Nodes and also supporting **SSH** connection for users who are not familiar with complicated VPS setups.

## 🌟 SSH protocol

Along with providing free private solutions for a wide range of users, I added this protocol to empower amateur users who have no knowledge of server configurations. It allows them to simply purchase a VPS in an emergency and connect via SSH with zero setup.  
Right now SSH proxies endure more than some modern protocols like reality on some ISPs in Iran for low bandwidth connections.  
It should be mentioned that SSH protocol only supports TCP traffic and you won't be able to use Telegram calls, Clubhouse etc.

## 🌟 Global Remote DNS

Merged all protocols' **Remote DNS** servers into one field in Global settings. VLESS now supports Cloudflare DNS servers and hijacks them into related DoH servers within worker.  
The Remote DNS only accepts IPv4 and IPv6 now to boost up performance specially for **VLESS**.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The worker scripts get updated in the background after you update to this version. however it needs to connect to the internet, You can confirm worker update by checking `Settings` > `VLESS` > `Cloudflare accounts`, there will be a manual update button in case the update was not successful.

## 💡 Bug fixes and improvements

- Added SSH protocol as it needs zero configuration skills for amateur users, supporting password, SSH key methods and Keep Alive settings.
- Enabled Psiphon, Tor and Chain proxy (except WireGuard and Hysteria2) for SSH connection.
- Made Remote DNS global, improved VLESS DNS performance and added Cloudflare DNS support to.
- Added Tor and Psiphon DNS servers as a fallback to Remote DNS.
- Added theme to config view page.
- Added config download button.
- Updated Log view page UI and added search box to it.
- Updated worker minification setup.
- Refactored the core logic.
- Fixed Tor and Psiphon routing bug in 1.2.2.
- Fixed scanner pause bug.
- Fixed log view lag.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/bia-pain-bache/BPB-VPN/compare/v1.2.1...v1.3.0

releases.title: BPB 1.2.0
releases.notes:
# 🎉 BPB VPN is here

Welcome to BPB VPN, a companion app designed to make setting up and using the BPB Panel and Wizard simpler and more approachable. From getting started to managing your VPN connection and even combining it with third-party proxies like Tor and Psiphon, my goal is to make the experience easier to follow and less of a hassle.

## 🌟 BPB Cloudflare scanners

BPB is now equipped with specific Cloudflare scanners for all protocol! The scanner follows user settings for protocol i.e. Fingerprint, SNI, IP version, Custom domain, Transport and is even capable of scanning with Fragment and UDP Obfuscation (ECH is excluded). Please note that the more `Probes count` you set, the better IPs you get, but the downside is the scanner consumes more worker requests during VLESS scanning.

## 🌟 Serverless DNS mode

We've already seen DNS clients like `Rethink`, now assume you have a full DNS client with traffic splitting and even DNS tester!
A very helpful feature which helps you through DNS disruptions supporting UDP,TCP,DoH and DoQ servers. You have your Workers and Pages DoH as private servers (using Cloudflare Security DoH as backend) along with some well-known public DNS servers of all types.

The lovely part of this feature is **Fake SNI servers**, it uses Cloudflare, Google and Quad9 DoH servers with a Fake whitelisted SNI.

## 💡 Bug fixes and Improvements

- Added **Snowflake AMP** to Tor modes.
- Added **Routing Strategy**.
- **Connection behaviour:** The app now checks the actual connection before updating the UI. As a result, connections that are not working remain in the `Connecting` state, unlike the usual behavior in v2rayNG and similar apps.
- Renamed **Serverless Fragment** to **Serverless Packet**, since it also supports UDP obfuscation.
- Updated the default **UDP obfuscation** noises to simulate the AmneziaWG obfuscation.
- Added **QUIC**, **DNS query**, **STUN Binding** mimic presets to UDP noises, along with a **None** mode to apply custom packet for **Expression** UDP noise mode.
- Changed the default Warp **Reserved bytes** value to disabled to reduce protocol fingerprinting on some ISPs.
- Added bilingual Github issue templates in Farsi and English. It worth mentioning that all BPB projects are handled by one person, so please only report technical bugs and misconfigurations (not the app performance on your ISP) with all requested info, issue gets closed ASAP otherwise.
- Updated **Reset settings** behaviour so that clean IPs and endpoints are preserved.
- Updated the **Domain Fronting** + **Psiphon** config, it has much better performance now and tries to keep [@Patterniha](https://github.com/patterniha) template safe.
- Updated the routing rules to block Iran firewall IPs by default.
- Updated Xray-core to v26.11.9
- Updated Tor to v4.9.16
- Added ECH retries to Cloudflare API calls.
- Added **Serverless DNS** mode supporting UDP,TCP,DoH and DoQ servers. Private servers use Cloudflare Security DoH as backend.
- Added **Prefer IPv6** option.
- Updated routing rules.
- Added Fake SNI DoH feat. to DNS mode.
- Updated Fragment default setting, for now it may works on some ISPs.
- Fixed the BPB quick settings tile bug #9
- Fixed UI and documentation bugs #13 #14

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Some default settings have been changed since 1.0.0 and 1.1.0, so I recommend to reset settings after this update just to be sure. Don't worry, this will preserve your clean IPs and endpoints.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/bia-pain-bache/BPB-VPN/compare/v1.0.0...v1.2.0

## گروه‌های لحظه‌ای مثل تلگرام، خبر پاسخ و سنجاق، و اینترنت و باتری کمتر در گره

### افزوده‌شده
- **گره: گروه‌ها و کانال‌ها لحظه‌ای، مثل تلگرام.** پست، واکنش، حذف، ویرایش و رأی در گروه‌ها و کانال‌ها، و تغییر دسترسی‌ها مثل باز کردن «ارسال پیام»، حالا همان لحظه از راه دو سرور ایران گره به اعضا می‌رسد، بی آنکه برای هر عضو جدا فرستاده شود. سرور ایران همیشه اول است؛ صندوق گوگل و راه‌های دیگر فقط وقتی به کار می‌آیند که سرور ایران در دسترس نباشد. عضوی که مدتی دور بود، پست‌های جامانده را از سرور ایران می‌خواند. عضوهایی که هنوز نسخهٔ قدیمی دارند مثل قبل پیام می‌گیرند، کندتر.
- **گره: خبر پاسخ و نام شما در گروه، مثل تلگرام.** وقتی کسی در گروه یا گروه رسمی روی پیام شما پاسخ می‌دهد یا نام شما را با @ می‌نویسد، اعلان می‌آید، حتی اگر گروه بی‌صدا باشد، و تا آن را نبینید کنار گروه در فهرست گفت‌وگوها @ دیده می‌شود. پیش‌تر هیچ چیز نمی‌گفت که کسی جواب شما را داده است.
- **گره: سنجاق با خبرش.** وقتی پیامی در گروه، کانال، گفت‌وگوی تکی یا کانال و گروه رسمی سنجاق می‌شود، سطر «… سنجاق کرد» در گفت‌وگو می‌آید و اعلانش هم می‌رسد، مثل تلگرام؛ در گروه بی‌صدا هم، مگر «پیام‌های سنجاق‌شده» را در تنظیمات اعلان خاموش کنید. در کانال، سنجاق به نام خود کانال است. پیش‌تر سنجاق بی‌صدا بالای گفت‌وگو می‌نشست و کسی باخبر نمی‌شد.
- **گره: اینترنت و باتری کمتر.** وقتی سرور ایران گره در دسترس است، گره بیرون از برنامه هر ۵ دقیقه یک بار به صندوق گوگل سر می‌زند (پیش‌تر هر ۳۰ تا ۹۰ ثانیه)، پیامی را که صندوق گیرنده گم کرده بود دیگر پشت سر هم و تا یک هفته دوباره نمی‌فرستد، اتصال مستقیم گوشی‌به‌گوشی را آرام‌تر جست‌وجو می‌کند، و کانال و گروه رسمی را هر ۳ ساعت یک بار همگام می‌کند نه هر ۱۰ دقیقه. چیزی دیرتر نمی‌رسد، چون پیام‌ها از راه سرور ایران همان لحظه می‌رسند.
- **کانفیگ‌های ایران: سرورلس نسخهٔ ۵۹.** کانفیگ‌های ایران حالا نسخهٔ ۵۹ سرورلس ‎@patterniha را هم دارند: «oob»، «fragA» و «fragB»، هر کدام با DNS گوگل، کلادفلر یا AdGuard هم، روی هستهٔ Xray خود سازنده نسخهٔ 26.11.12 برای گوشی‌های ۶۴ و ۳۲ بیتی. کانفیگ‌های قبلی سر جایشان هستند.

### رفع‌شده
- **گره: «اجازهٔ ارسال پیام» در گروه ذخیره نمی‌شد.** مالک گروه در دسترسی‌ها «ارسال پیام» را برای اعضا باز می‌کرد و ذخیره می‌زد، ولی گروه بسته می‌ماند و اعضا «نوشتن پیام در این گروه مجاز نیست» می‌دیدند. حالا همان بار اول ذخیره می‌شود و اعضا همان لحظه می‌توانند بفرستند. همین ایراد گاهی پیوستن تازه‌واردها را هم بی‌صدا رد می‌کرد؛ آن هم درست شد.
- **گره: پیام‌ها روی بعضی گوشی‌ها بار نمی‌شد.** روی گوشی‌ای که منتظر پیوستن به چند گروه بود، گره پیوسته سرگرم همان کار می‌ماند و پیام‌ها و گفت‌وگوها دیر یا اصلاً باز نمی‌شدند. حالا این کار سبک شده و گفت‌وگوها زود باز می‌شوند.
- **گره: جست‌وجوی @نام گروه.** جست‌وجوی نام گروهی که در آن عضوید، مثل ‎@mlmwindows، گاهی صفحهٔ «افزودن کانال تلگرام» را باز می‌کرد، و گروه‌هایی که عضوشان بودید با @نامشان پیدا نمی‌شدند. حالا خود گروه پیدا و باز می‌شود.
- **فنیکس: خطا برطرف شد.** خطایی که فنیکس را از وصل شدن بازمی‌داشت برطرف شد.
- **پایداری: ده‌ها کرش و یخ‌زدگی گزارش‌شده درست شد.** از گزارش‌های خودکار کرش نسخه‌های ۱.۲.۴۷ و ۱.۲.۴۸: باز شدن گره پس از خطای هسته، جست‌وجو و نمایش عکس در گره، صفحهٔ پروفایل، ایمیل کلادفلری که نویسهٔ نامرئی داشت، سرویس‌های اسکن روی اندروید ۱۳ و پایین‌تر، مامی روی اندروید ۷، لنترن، نشان شمار پیام روی گوشی‌های سونی و نقشه در گفت‌وگو دیگر برنامه را نمی‌بندند. کارهای سنگین شروع برنامه، کاشی‌های خانه، ویجت‌ها، قطع OpenVPN، «باز شد» در MAE و آزمون گروهی کانفیگ‌ها از رشتهٔ اصلی بیرون رفت تا صفحه روی گوشی‌های ضعیف یخ نزند، و سقف حافظهٔ برنامه مثل خود تلگرام بالاتر رفت.

### کدام فایل را دانلود کنم؟
- **arm64-v8a:** بیشتر گوشی‌ها (۶۴ بیتی). اگر نمی‌دانید، همین را بگیرید.
- **armeabi-v7a:** گوشی‌های قدیمی‌تر ۳۲ بیتی.
- **universal:** روی همهٔ گوشی‌ها نصب می‌شود، ولی حجمش بیشتر است.
- به‌روزرسانی از داخل خود برنامه فایل درستِ گوشی شما را خودش برمی‌دارد.

- Fix regressions introduced in the previous version.
- Change the name of the Quick Settings tile to app name.

- Improve file verification of the route asset updater (by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)). Before replacing the old files, for preset route asset providers, SHA-256 checksum is verified; for all files, the basic file structure is validated.
- Publish shortcuts dynamically to better work with some automation tools (#516, by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)).
- Many fixes for share link import and export (by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)).
- Fix connection failure caused by clearing the cache of the app.
- Fix some REALITY fingerprint values in UI not matching with the actual values.

- Update Go to 1.27.4 and ML-DSA is no longer advertised in `signature_algorithm_cert` in TLS Client Hello. Exclave's non-uTLS REALITY implementation also no longer advertises ML-DSA in `signature_algorithm_cert` to match the behavior of Go TLS.
- Update uTLS to latest commit and fingerprint "Chrome" now matches Chrome 155. uTLS latest commit requires Go 1.27, so Go 1.26 support is dropped and compiling Exclave now requires at least Go 1.27.
- For Snell protocol, domain address is no longer resolved to IP when sending UDP packets.
- Update Mozilla CA certificate store and 6 CA certificates are removed.
- The memory usage of rule matcher is reduced (maybe).

- Ignore certificates that can't be parsed by Go in AndroidCAstore (e.g. certificates with [negative serial number](https://crt.sh/?q=28903A635B5280FAE6774C0B6DA7D6BAA64AF2E8)).
- Fix chain proxy with the combination of some protocols unable to connect.
- Add [developer options](https://github.com/ExclaveNetwork/Exclave/wiki/Experiments) to set GODEBUG and environment variables for the Go library. They are set after Go runtime initialization, therefore not all GODEBUG and environment variables can take effect.
- Re-enable R8 optimizations for the legacy flavor.
- Update Java version from 21 to 25.

---

About CVE-2026-98432 ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-98432), [golang-announce](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/PCoQcdxoScw)):

- Almost all the Linux kernels used by Android devices come without MPTCP support, so it is a no-op to disable MPTCP.
- Mitigating the vulnerability by disabling MPTCP is not the appropriate way. While the demonstrated exploit requires MPTCP, the underlying bug resides within TCP and is not specific to MPTCP. The fix for this vulnerability is to upgrade to a patched kernel version. Even if this vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling MPTCP, an outdated kernel is still vulnerable to tons of other RCE vulnerabilities.
- Therefore, Exclave will not explicitly disable MPTCP like many other proxy software and network tools written in Go.
- If you did compile the kernel with MPTCP support, or you insist that MPTCP must be explicitly disabled like some other Go-written software, set the related GODEBUG value through developer options yourself.

- Fix high CPU usage after proxy closed or network switching for Hysteria 2 (maybe other QUIC-based protocols too).
- Fix connections not closed correctly on proxy closed.
- Fix the `/proc/net/` based UID dumper on Android 9 or earlier (similar to https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/commit/40bc411e8d024e3f8c8f435c2a2ad5e4c0e04bce).

- Add experimental CONNECT-IP (so-called "MASQUE") support.
- Fix CONNECT-UDP bugs.
- Update Go to 1.27.3, which has been hardcoded to blacklist 8 eMudhra intermediate certificates.
- Update the bundled Mozilla CA certificate store to the latest version, which has removed eMudhra root certificates.
- Rename root CA provider "system" to "Go" and rename root CA provider "system and user" to "Android" to avoid confusion.

This is a security update. The private keys for some of eMudhra’s intermediate certificates are too weak, causing them to be [compromised](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/) through enumeration and exposing users to man-in-the-middle attacks. These private keys have since spread across the Internet and can be obtained by everyone.

You may want to know the impact of the compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates for Exclave: https://github.com/ExclaveNetwork/Exclave/issues/500.

These APKs were compiled and signed by this workflow run, from the

## ArasClient v1.8.6

- **Aether core 2.4.0** — official binaries for all ABIs, checker-verified; TLS-fingerprint flags and WARP API settings (address / server name / host) up to date with the core, and the editor gained the two names of the Cloudflare API as pickable options
- **Chain-end reporting** — when Tor or Psiphon inside the tunnel ends, the core stops itself; the app now watches for it, stops the session, and tells you in a toast instead of hanging on a dead listener
- **Warm-up listener fix** — a kept-connection SOCKS5 greeting probe counts each served listener once, so long Psiphon/Tor warm-ups no longer queue up on connection attempts
- **Session port protection** — hand-written commands with invalid / unreachable / shared / taken listener addresses are refused before the core starts
- **VPN polish** — IPv6 on by default with automatic IPv4 fallback, DNS family filter + safe fallback, MTU trim/guard, builder-in-try
- **Subscription panels** — Support-Url and Profile-Web-Page-Url headers parsed (http/https/tg only), info bar buttons for support link and panel page, and the main list refreshes after subscriptions update

releases.title: ArasClient v1.8.2
releases.notes:
# ArasClient v1.8.2

Two rounds since **v1.8.1**: the ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) work for the
Xray profiles, and WireGuard/AmneziaWG dialled by the core like every other
protocol. Everything from v1.8.1 and earlier is described in the
[v1.8.1 release notes](https://github.com/ArasTey/ArasClient/releases/tag/v1.8.1).

## 🕵️ ECH: the key lookup can now ride through its own outbound

Plain-DNS ECH key lookups are being blocked in some places while ECH itself
still works (cloudflare-ech.com answers). The lookup needs a path of its own,
and the app now has one:

- **Two fields on TLS profiles** (VMess / VLESS / Shadowsocks / Trojan, and
  Hysteria2): `echConfigList` — the key source — and **`echOutbound`**, the ECH
  outbound as raw JSON. The Aether profiles keep their own ECH fields (ECH DNS
  / ECH domain) from v1.8.1; this one is for the Xray protocols.
- **The recipe** (from the core's author):

  ```json
  echConfigList: h2c://1.1.1.1/dns-query
  ```

  ```json
  echOutbound:
  {"tag":"tls-repack-dns","protocol":"freedom","settings":{"redirect":"1.1.1.1:443"},"streamSettings":{"security":"tls","tlsSettings":{"serverName":"www.microsoft.com","verifyPeerCertByName":"fromMitm,www.microsoft.com","alpn":["fromMitm"],"fingerprint":"chrome"}}}
  ```

- **What the app does with it**: the ECH outbound is appended to the generated
  configuration exactly as written, and the profile's TLS settings get
  `echSockopt.dialerProxy` pointing at it — so the ECH key query leaves
  through that masked outbound (a TLS connection to a public resolver with a
  borrowed SNI and a certificate checked by name) instead of a plain DNS
  query. The profile's own handshake then uses the fetched key, and the real
  server name stays hidden.
- **The guards**: the ECH outbound must be a JSON object, must come with an
  echConfigList, and needs a tag of its own — not `direct`, `block` or
  `exit-node`, and not starting with `proxy` (balancers pick their members by
  that prefix). Two different ECH outbounds written under the same tag get
  numbered (`tag-2`); a tag another outbound already uses is refused; an
  imported ECH outbound that was never checked fails the connection instead of
  letting the query go out in the clear. The ECH outbound is a TLS-only
  setting — a REALITY profile keeps it unused. Same rules as PattNG P67.
- **No core rebuild was needed**: the bundled Xray core (patterniha v26.10.13)
  already carries the ECH-over-h2c lookup, the `echSockopt` and the `fromMitm`
  certificate-by-name support — the app-side plumbing was the missing half.

## 🔌 WireGuard and AmneziaWG, dialled by the core like every other protocol

- **AmneziaWG was bypassing the core.** The selected AWG profile took the
  VpnService TUN descriptor for itself, so the tunnel came up carrying nothing:
  no DNS, no routing, no statistics — while the latency test of the same
  profile went through the core. The standalone tunnel is gone: every
  protocol, AmneziaWG included, is dialled by the core now, and the TUN has one
  reader again.
- **Plain WireGuard** had no keep-alive (the peer's mapping expires after
  minutes) and left `noKernelTun` unset — in root mode the core then built a
  kernel TUN that fought the app's own interface. Both are filled in now, with
  the allowed IPs and the keep-alive.
- **The `.conf` parsers** no longer cut an IPv6 endpoint in half and no longer
  drop `PersistentKeepalive`.

## 🔧 In this release

- The bundled core AAR was rebuilt from the same pinned core tag
  (`aras-core-26.10.13`); the core source itself did not change.
- The five APKs are the same size as v1.8.1's (the ECH work is a few lines of
  code; the rebuilt core library differs by 40 KB).

## 🔐 Signing

- Signed with the dedicated ArasClient key — **the same key as v1.7.10 and
  v1.8.1** (certificate SHA-256 `3b2a6fa9…b5ba`): all five APKs, one signer
  each. Upgrades install over v1.8.1 without uninstalling.

## ⚠️ Known limitations

- The ECH outbound is used on TLS profiles only, and the recipe's `fromMitm`
  certificate check relies on the core's fromMitm support — present in the
  bundled core.
- Profiles imported with a broken older build keep wrong AWG values: config
  fixes change parsing, not stored data. If AWG still fails after updating,
  **delete the profile and re-import the `.conf` file**.
- **OpenVPN is not included.** The official path is integrating with the
  installed OpenVPN for Android via its intent/AIDL API — planned as its own
  release.
- The Psiphon/Aether/Mieru tunnel path is not re-verified on a device for this
  release's cores yet (the network blocked handshakes during testing; the old
  and the new cores behaved identically under the same conditions, so no
  regression is suspected).
- Release builds log at `warning` level by default — set the log level to Info
  in Settings before reporting a VPN problem.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.8.1
releases.notes:
# ArasClient v1.8.1

Everything below is **every change since v1.7.10** — the releases v1.8.0 and
v1.8.1 listed in one place. v1.8.1 on top of v1.8.0 fixes the delay numbers,
and adds the exit node, sing-box imports and the TLS fingerprints.

## 🛜 AmneziaWG actually works now (the headline of 1.8.0)

AmneziaWG profiles **never carried traffic** before v1.8.0. Five defects were
stacked to hide it, all fixed:

1. **Mimic packets (I1–I5) reach the core.** Decoys sent ahead of every
   handshake initiation so the first bytes on the wire belong to another
   protocol (e.g. an "OPTIONS sip:…" line). Configured per profile in the AWG
   editor; a spec the core cannot parse fails validation at edit time instead
   of silently killing the tunnel at connect.
2. **Junk params are read from `[Interface]`.** AmneziaVPN writes
   `Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1/S2/H1–H4` as device-level settings; the old parser read
   them in peer context, found nothing, and silently substituted stock values
   — the server dropped every packet. Now `[Interface]` first, `[Peer]`
   fallback.
3. **`.conf` detection no longer depends on the exact spelling of `Jc`.**
   Files are classified as Amnezia on the key set, case-insensitively
   (including S3/S4 and I1–I5).
4. **The TUN descriptor has one reader.** tun2socks used to win the race and
   drain packets into a SOCKS proxy nothing serves in AWG mode.
5. **An entry proxy that is Aether/Mieru no longer marks a whole subscription
   −1.** The daemons now start when a chain needs them (refcounted), and the
   latency test no longer probes a chained profile's server directly.

Verified end-to-end on an emulator: tunnel up, junk params matching the file,
mimic packets emitted, traffic crossing the tun interface across repeated
on/off cycles.

## 📶 Ping and delay fixes (the point of 1.8.1)

- **Delay numbers read ~5× too high in v1.8.0 — fixed.** A v1.8.0 change made
  every measurement a single cold request: it paid the wireguard handshake +
  TCP + TLS (≈4–5 round trips) instead of one round trip on a warm
  connection. A server whose real delay was ~100 ms displayed ~500 ms.
  The measurement is back to the v1.7.x semantics: two samples over the same
  connection, min kept — the first warms the path, the second reads one real
  RTT.
- **"Ping all" reports the egress country on cards now.** A new core shim
  carries the country/IP back through the same dial path as the delay test,
  so batch results fill the card flags without separate requests.
- **Tests start immediately** instead of waiting behind a GeoIP pre-warm
  (DNS + batch lookup) that used to run before the first ping was dispatched.
- **No more dropped frames during long test runs.** Each result patches its
  own card; the whole group is no longer rebuilt (and every profile
  re-decoded) once per result.

## 📝 Remarks are yours

- **Provider flags in remarks are kept** on import: nothing rewrites a
  non-empty remark any more; default names only fill an empty one. Cards
  still compose their own flag, so nothing renders twice.

## 🚪 Exit node (new in 1.8.1)

In the Aether editor you can now pick **which config the tunnel dials out
through** — the list shows your profiles, the same way a proxy chain does:

- Leave it blank and the tunnel leaves directly (freedom), as always.
- Name a profile and the aether core's own dialer goes through the app's core
  to that profile's outbound — a chain pinned to the exit side.
- A name that no longer matches exactly one profile never breaks the
  connect: it degrades to the direct exit, and the editor shows what it
  picked.
- Latency tests of exit-node profiles serialize, because each owns the loop
  back port while it runs.

## 🧩 Core updated to patterniha v26.10.13

The bundled Xray core moved to patterniha's v26.10.13 base with our AmneziaWG
patches carried over (+91 upstream commits over v1.8.0's base), notably:

- **TUN inbound** uses Xray's built-in lightweight TCP/IP stack (gVisor
  removed) with several stability fixes.
- **MASQUE**: XMUX support, WARP domain-fronting fixes, Chrome User-Agent.
- **TLS**: Xray's built-in RootCAs by default (defends against a maliciously
  injected system CA), more ECH hardening.
- **Lua scripting** for `dns` and `routing` (power users).
- `allowInsecure` keeps working on public servers (restored for legacy
  profiles since the 26.x cores removed it).
- The fingerprint picker gains `hellochrome_120/131/133`,
  `hellofirefox_120/148`.

## 🌐 Root mode

- **DNS leak fix for LAN-to-ISP resolvers** (ported from upstream #6298): DNS
  queries to private/LAN resolvers are DNAT'd to a public IP so they resolve
  through the configured remote DNS instead of leaking back to the LAN/ISP
  resolver — the "some sites work, some don't" symptom.

## 🪂 Aether core updated to the official v2.3.0

`libaether.so` (arm64 / armeabi-v7a / x86_64) now carries the official
CluvexStudio Aether v2.3.0 release binaries, checksums verified against the
release's SHA256SUMS.txt. With it, and matching PattNG's editor:

- **MASQUE SNI** — the name the MASQUE handshakes put in their ClientHello.
- **Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)** with its lookup resolver (`ECH DNS`) and
  key domain (`ECH domain`).
- **Four TLS fingerprints** — Chrome (default), Firefox, Semi-Python, Go:
  the core offers the captured client's TLS 1.2 suite order and drops GREASE
  where that client sends none.
- **WireGuard-over-MASQUE (gool)**, **MASQUE-in-MASQUE (mim)**, **WARP-in-WARP
  (wiw)** — two-hop tunnels with outer and inner gateways, as before.
- **warp→Psiphon, Psiphon→warp, Psiphon-only** — the three carrier modes,
  with Psiphon region support.
- The **exit node** picker above is an Aether editor feature too.

## 📥 sing-box subscriptions (.json) now import

An update to a sing-box `.json` sublink used to import nothing. The
converter reads the dialing outbounds — **vless** (including REALITY's
public key / short id / fingerprint), **vmess**, **trojan**,
**shadowsocks**, **hysteria2** — into the same share links the app has al-
ways read, skips group/meta objects (selector, urltest, direct, block, dns),
and validates the whole list before touching storage. Manual imports and
subscription updates both take it.

## 🔧 Infrastructure & fixes

- **Release signing restored in CI** — the workflow step that restores the
  keystore was missing the secrets mapping since the key hardening, so every
  automated build had failed with `KEYSTORE_B64: unbound variable`. CI now
  builds, signs, and uploads end-to-end (verified green).
- The main menu sheet (the three-line menu) no longer bounces up and down
  when dragged hard; it is pinned to the expanded position with an inner
  scroll.
- Subscription traffic display accepts a `used=` key, which some panels send
  instead of `upload`/`download`.
- This release is signed with the dedicated ArasClient key — **the same key
  as v1.7.10** and every release before it that carried it: all five APKs,
  one signer each. Upgrades install without uninstalling.

## ⚠️ Known limitations

- **Profiles imported with a broken older build keep wrong AWG values.**
  Config fixes change parsing, not stored data. If AWG still fails after
  updating: **delete the profile and re-import the `.conf` file.**
- **OpenVPN is not included.** The official path is integrating with the
  installed OpenVPN for Android via its intent/AIDL API — planned as its own
  release.
- The bundled Psiphon server list (427 entries) is verified against
  Psiphon's signing key on every use, and the client fetches a fresh list
  itself once it has network. The full Psiphon/Aether/Mieru tunnel path is
  not re-verified on a device for this release's new cores yet (the network
  blocked handshakes during testing; the old and new cores behaved
  identically under the same conditions, so no regression is suspected).
- Release builds log at `warning` level by default — set the log level to
  Info in Settings before reporting a VPN problem.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.7.10
releases.notes:
ArasClient v1.7.10

Adds Mieru gateway profiles and rebuilds the connect button. The core is unchanged from v1.7.9.

### Persian layout

The top bar draws the wordmark as two texts — "Aras" and "Client" — side by side in a row. In a
Persian layout that row lays out right to left, so the halves swapped and the title read
**"ClientAras"**. The wordmark is now pinned left to right: a brand reads the same in every language.
Where the app name appears as a single string it is wrapped in a directional isolate instead, and
deliberately not where it builds a file name, since those marks would otherwise end up in the path.

**134 strings had no Persian translation**, so the whole Aether and Mieru editor, the `.arasc` export
screen, the stats screen and the menu sections fell back to English inside a Persian interface. All
134 are translated; the Persian locale now carries every string the default one does.

### Mieru

Mieru is a separate client process that holds the tunnel and serves a local SOCKS, so a Mieru
profile is carried by a SOCKS hop to that listener — the same shape an Aether profile already has.
No core work was needed: Mieru ships a native Android build.

- Add a Mieru profile manually from the import menu, or import a `mieru://` link
- Round-trips through `.arasc` like every other profile type
- The client is taken from enfein/mieru v3.38.0, checksum verified against the release

**A Mieru client left behind by a killed app is now reaped before a start.** This is not tidiness: a
survivor keeps the loopback port, and the next start then dies with `address already in use` rather
than starting at all.

**Mieru is arm64 only.** That is the only Android build published, so the editor reports the client as
absent on an `armeabi-v7a` or `x86_64` device rather than failing obscurely. It adds about 14 MB to
the arm64 split.

### Connect button

The connect button is rebuilt. It was a flat rounded box that distinguished connected from stopped by
nothing but the glyph changing.

Everything that glows is now drawn inside the circle: the rotating sweep is inset to the rim and
clipped by the shape, and the breathing light is a radial gradient that is transparent in the middle.
Nothing spills past the outline, so the button keeps a clean edge against the bar behind it.

The rotation and the breath run only while the tunnel is up, and the entry spring fires once on the
way to connected, so an idle button costs nothing.

### Size

The arm64 split is about 52 MB and the universal about 140 MB. The other splits are unchanged.

### Tests

178. The Mieru configuration is checked by parsing it: a password containing a quote, a backslash and
a newline has to come back out exactly as it went in.

Still nothing here has been through a device test. If something misbehaves, the app's logcat screen
carries the Mieru client's own output.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.7.9
releases.notes:
ArasClient v1.7.9

A large release: the native core moves to patterniha/Xray-core v26.9.27, MASQUE and the
xdrive transport arrive, and Aether gateway profiles are supported end to end.

### Core

The core is rebuilt on patterniha/Xray-core v26.9.27, with every ArasClient patch carried
over: AnyTLS, the AmneziaWG 3.1 junk parameters, `allowInsecure` as a TLS field, and the
`domain_strategy` field that AmneziaWG needs. This is 26 patch releases of upstream work,
plus the MASQUE and xdrive transports, which the old 26.9.1 base predated.

### Fixed

Five config-generation bugs, each caught by tests added in this release:

- **AnyTLS did not work at all.** The outbound was emitted with a `tcp` transport and no
  `anytlsSettings`, because the transport was set where `populateTransportSettings`
  immediately overwrote it. AnyTLS now emits its own transport.
- **AmneziaWG obfuscation was missing on first connect.** The junk parameters were copied
  onto the peer before the defaults were applied to the profile, so a server that had never
  been saved with them tunnelled unobfuscated.
- **One malformed port could break every server.** A non-numeric or out-of-range port threw
  out of config generation, and its callers only guarded a null return — so a bad server in a
  policy group or chain took the whole configuration down. It is now skipped.
- **Hysteria2 share links lost their bandwidth limits** and the port-hopping interval.
- **AmneziaWG's H3 parameter vanished on share and import.**

When the core rejects a configuration, its own reason now reaches the screen instead of a
generic "failed to start", and the generated configuration is written to the log at error
level so a rejection is diagnosable from a release build.

### MASQUE and xdrive

`MASQUE` (IETF CONNECT-IP, RFC 9484) is supported and import-only: it arrives through a
`masque://` link, a pasted config, a QR code or a `.arasc` file, and is deliberately not in
the "Add manually" list. The `masque` and `xdrive` transports are in the transport picker of
any protocol that supports them.

### Aether

Aether gateway profiles are supported. The tunnel is dialled by the aether core, a child
process holding the WARP identity and the scanned endpoint, so a profile's outbound is a SOCKS
hop to its loopback listener. The core ships in the app as a native library, checksum-verified
against its release, together with Psiphon's client and Tor's pluggable transport.

Share links and `.arasc` files use aether's own vocabulary, so they move between ArasClient,
the Aether app and PattNG unchanged. The screen collects the protocol (WireGuard, MASQUE, or
either two-hop tunnel), scan mode, obfuscation, IP version, ClientHello fragmentation, ECH,
and Psiphon and Tor. Two pairings the core refuses are caught while editing rather than at
connect time: either carrier in reverse needs MASQUE, and the two go together only nested.

**A WARP gateway usually does not answer a plain ping, and its exit address reads as Iranian.
Both are expected** — judge these profiles by whether they connect, not by the ping column.

**This release is larger than usual: about 54 MB of native library per ABI.**

### Build and tests

CI previously assembled the release APK and nothing else — the test suite never ran. It now
runs the unit tests and lint, and asserts against the built core that AnyTLS and AmneziaWG are
present and stock WireGuard is not, since a patch that fails to apply still produces a working
library, just one missing a feature. The core checkout is pinned by tag, so a release builds
the same core it was tested against.

The suite grew from 17 tests to 170.

releases.notes:
## What's Changed

ArasClient v1.7.5 brings the accumulated subscription, connectivity, diagnostics, and Quick Settings improvements developed since v1.7.0.

### Subscription Management

- Added a selected-subscription action that updates the subscription, runs a real ping test, sorts the results, and connects to the fastest reachable server.
- Added **Ping all in this subscription** directly to the selected subscription action box beside Edit, Update, Copy, and Delete.
- Improved Clash YAML parsing, including configuration-key ordering and UTF-8 BOM handling.
- Corrected Shadowsocks parsing for configurations using the `v2ray-plugin` option.
- Made Free-subscription replacement transactional so an interrupted update does not leave a partially replaced profile set.
- Improved subscription import/export handling, profile replacement, URL/clipboard import flows, and subscription navigation.
- Added shared subscription-workflow locking so update operations cannot race across the UI and daemon processes.
- Improved Free-subscription synchronization and reduced repeated failed retry work with a persisted cooldown.

### Connection Diagnostics

- Persist the real connection-ping delay, country code, IP address, and test timestamp for each profile.
- Prefer the country measured by the current connection ping on profile cards, with GeoIP and configuration-name fallbacks when no current measurement is available.
- Improved country/flag resolution and legacy serialization compatibility.
- Added unit coverage for country persistence, legacy delay records, and ping-country precedence.

### Quick Settings

- Added a complete **Update & Connect** Quick Settings workflow with progress, completion, and failure states.
- Added clear, distinct iconography for the Connect/Disconnect and Update/Connect actions.
- Made Update/Connect a true toggle: a second tap stops the running workflow and connected client and returns the tile to its ready state.
- Made Connect/Disconnect follow the actual core state, show the running server while connected, and return to an inactive state when stopped.
- Corrected Quick Settings service discovery metadata and preserved active state across tile-service recreation.
- Kept the launcher shortcut path as an additional quick-access route.

### Reliability and Performance

- Prevented duplicate Activity initialization work during recreation.
- Improved subscription update cancellation and daemon workflow cleanup.
- Improved card-rendering performance and reduced unnecessary UI work during subscription and connection updates.
- Preserved existing VPN, proxy, root, browser-dialer, and AmneziaWG functionality while extending the Quick Actions workflow.

### Documentation

- Updated the project README and release-facing documentation for the new subscription and Quick Actions capabilities.

### Validation

- Debug and release APK builds pass.
- The full debug unit-test suite passes.
- Release lintVital passes.
- All release variants are generated for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86, x86_64, and universal APK delivery.
- The GitHub release workflow rebuilds the native core bindings and release APKs from the configured upstream sources before attaching the artifacts.

## Shroudly 2.6.88

**Windows: Advanced mode asks for the administrator's permission once, not at every start of the computer; Games and apps mode comes on even when Windows is slow at startup; an antivirus that blocks PowerShell no longer gets it started over and over.**

### Windows (Advanced mode)
- Every start of the Advanced engine was a permission prompt (UAC, "shroudly-core-adv.exe"): at every start of the computer, and again whenever the engine had ended. Since 2.6.87 a game or a Stop no longer ends it; now the prompt itself is answered once. The engine started through it copies itself and WinDivert's files to `Common Files\Shroudly\advanced`, a folder only an administrator can write, and registers a scheduled task that runs that copy for this user only, on demand. From then on Shroudly starts Advanced mode through the task, with no prompt. It asks again, once, only after an update that changed the engine, or when the task is gone; whatever goes wrong on this way (a policy, an antivirus) ends in the prompt, as before.
- What the engine started this way does is not the caller's to say: it takes its options from a request file and accepts only the packet options, each checked; it writes its status only into its own folder, a new file every time; in the user's folder it only reads. Uninstalling Shroudly removes the task and the copies.
- The engine opens no console window of its own.
- A prompt nobody answered for three minutes (the computer started with no one at it) is said as that; it used to read "Advanced mode failed: #< CLIXML".

### Windows (Games and apps mode, Roblox)
- On a computer still starting up, with an antivirus looking at every new program, Windows' registry tool took longer than its four seconds, and Games and apps mode was refused for the whole session ("this session has no volatile environment"): Roblox opened with no way to the internet ("critical settings could not be downloaded", a report from Türkiye). ## Shroudly 2.6.83

**Blocked sites open faster: a new one starts with what already opened other blocked sites on the network, the names of one service share what one of them finds, and a technique that keeps working is not checked again after a restart; new techniques (several TLS records, random-size segments, an urgent byte with a record cut, new cut places in the domain's own label, HTTP Host rewrites); Advanced mode gets a stronger way for servers nothing else opens and steps aside before a game's anti-cheat looks; remote settings fall back to their mirror.**

### Every system
- A blocked site the engine had never seen started with the untouched request, and behind a filter that drops without a word that was a second or more of silence before any technique, then the list a batch at a time, for every new name (a report from Türk Telekom: blocked sites opened visibly later than with a tool that applies one fixed method to everything, while the line itself was as fast through Shroudly as without it). Now, once one technique has opened two different blocked sites on this network, a new name races it against the untouched request: the untouched request still goes first with a short moment to itself, so a site that is not blocked goes untouched as before. It is forgotten when the network changes, and nothing is learned from it unless the untouched request is shown blocked.
- Names of one site or service opened at once share what one of them finds (YouTube's video servers and images, Discord's domains, Instagram's, X's), instead of each walking the list on its own.
- A learned technique is checked again half an hour after it last opened the site, not half an hour after it was learned: after a restart or a network change, sites learned earlier no longer race the untouched request on their first connection. A block that was lifted is still found.
- New techniques in Auto, at the end of the list so nothing before them moves: an urgent byte after the first and the record cut five bytes before the name's end (what many Türk Telekom users run), the same cut after a one-byte split, and a record cut in the middle of the domain's own label. New cut places for that label (googlevideo in rr3---sn-x.googlevideo.com), where a cut in the middle of a long CDN name fell in the subdomain. A batch of the search holds one more technique, so a name nothing opens still reaches the last way out no later than before.
- New fixed choices in Settings, applied to every site from the first packet: several TLS records, small random pieces, an urgent byte with a record cut. They are not in Auto's list: every technique added there is one more a site nothing opens walks before the last way out.
- Plain HTTP: Host header rewrites every server tried took (lower-case header name, mixed-case host, no space), tried only on HTTP connections.
- A newly opened blocked site's line says how long it took ("opened with X (3 tries, ipv4, 2.4 s)").
- Remote settings ask each source in turn until one gives a usable file: a file whose signature does not check (a mirror out of step, a captive portal's page), expired or older no longer ends the check at the first source.

### Windows, macOS and Linux
- Advanced mode steps aside as soon as a game's anti-cheat bootstrapper starts (Fortnite's launcher and Easy Anti-Cheat's _EAC_EOS program; BattlEye's _BE launchers): it used to wait for the service and the game to be seen together, after the anti-cheat had already scanned the drivers, and Fortnite kicked a player for a "forbidden tool".
- Advanced mode: a server whose decoyed first segment goes out again unanswered gets a stronger way for ten minutes: the decoy eight times, kept from the server by the TCP timestamp where the connection has one, and the real ClientHello cut after its first byte with the decoy's ClientHello in front of it (what opened YouTube's video servers on Rostelecom). Every other server goes exactly as before; the seqovl part is never larger than the real segment, for PPPoE lines.

### Android
- An update download that timed out on every source is tried once more through the engine, then directly.

## Shroudly 2.6.82

**Tor starts again on Android; with QUIC off, calls and games on UDP 443 go through again; no country taken from a remembered shutdown where the time zone names another; signed remote settings, so a technique, a Tor bridge or a rule can change without a new version; the store copies follow the stores' rules on helping others.** (2.6.81 was not released on its own: everything of it is here.)

### Android

### Android, iPhone, iPad and the Mac
- QUIC turned off dropped every datagram to UDP port 443, which cut what uses that port for itself, calls' relays among them (WhatsApp calls stuck on "connecting"). Now only a flow that starts as QUIC is turned away (its Initial answered, as in 2.6.80); anything else on 443 goes as any UDP does.

- A country remembered from a shutdown is used only where the time zone names no place (UTC and the like), and a site of a listed country answering alone counts as a national-only network only where the time zone is that country's: a phone in Qatar had kept Iranian decoy names.

**QUIC turned off is refused on the spot on every system; the country is read from the time zone first; "Something not working?" only after Shroudly itself went wrong; a Roblox installer from the browser goes through Shroudly by itself; Tor 16.0.1.**
